purpose: Each mutant is the SAME isolation candidate (fixtures/model.mjs) with EXACTLY ONE cross-tenant isolation gate removed — modeling a real attack from the W0 ledger §3 RED-line table (docs/specs/2026-07-03-rr-isolation-invariants.md). With the gate gone, the cross-tenant attack it stops SUCCEEDS (the candidate returns ALLOW where the fixed all-DENY acceptance oracle demands DENY), so run.sh goes RED and reports the attack that succeeded as first_divergence. `bin/falsify rr-multitenant-isolation` runs the golden (expect PASS — every attack DENIED) then every mutant (expect REJECT — the dropped gate's attack caught). Falsifiability score = mutants rejected / total, conditioned on golden passing; this P0 isolation gate requires 1.0. A surviving mutant would prove an isolation gate is NOT load-bearing and BLOCKS the build. This is the meta-proof the multi-tenant isolation is real, not tautological: drop any gate -> the oracle goes RED.
candidate_contract: An ES module exporting default function evaluate(attackId) -> 'DENY' | 'ALLOW' for each cross-tenant attack id in the acceptance oracle. run.sh imports the candidate and grades evaluate(attackId) against every case (all expected 'DENY'), reporting the FIRST attack that returned ALLOW as first_divergence {file, step, expected:'DENY', actual:'ALLOW'}.

mutants.attack_that_succeeds: A1/A5 IDOR via repo slug — team A dispatches team B's repo
mutants.reject_contract: attack A1-idor-repo: expected DENY, candidate returns ALLOW -> gate status=fail at step 'A1-idor-repo'
